desc: Evaluate an integer arithmetic expression. First remove every space character from s; parse what remains. Grammar: expr = term, then zero or more of ("+" or "-") term; term = factor, then zero or more of ("*" or "/") factor; factor = a number (one or more decimal digits) or "(" expr ")". Operators of equal precedence group left to right; "/" divides and truncates toward zero. There is no unary minus. Syntax errors take priority: scanning left to right, at the first point where the next character cannot continue a valid expression, return the error "unexpected end" if the input has run out there, or "unexpected character: " followed by that character otherwise (this includes characters left over after a complete expression). Only if the whole input is syntactically valid, evaluate it; if any division has a right operand that evaluates to 0, return the error "division by zero".

decls.ts: type Result<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: string };
